subject: Request: Nimbus multi-year rate anchor + renewal escape clause approval
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood-inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Nimbus multi-year rate anchor + renewal escape clause approval

Team —

Quick ask: Nimbus Health is asking for a 3-year commitment with the following non-standard commercial terms. I need an exec sign-off (or clear do-not-approve) so I can finalize pricing with Procurement this week.

Deal snapshot:
- ACV: $1,200,000 year 1; expected annual growth built into usage.
- Proposed list discount: 38% (Net effective ~ $744k year 1)
- Term: 36 months, annual billing preferred by customer.

Non-standard asks from Nimbus (high level):
1) Rate anchor: Lock their blended unit rate for the 36-month term (no upward list-rate changes inside term).
2) Uplift cap: If model-serving costs increase, we apply an annual uplift capped at +6% per year (compounding).
3) Renewal protection / \"escape clause\": If Nimbus’s total committed spend falls >30% at any renewal, they may exit without penalty or convert to month-to-month at the then-current list pricing.

Rationale for approval:
- Strategic: Nimbus is evaluating platform-wide LLM adoption across 12 hospitals; significant cross-sell/expansion upside.
- Competitive: Their procurement asked for price certainty to justify internal budget approvals across multiple orgs.
- Technical: We can operationally support their SLOs on Dedicated capacity.

Risks / mitigations:
- Revenue protection: The escape clause creates churn risk at renewal. Recommend a 60-day notification requirement + 90-day transition assistance and commit to preserved usage credits for 6 months post-exit to reduce abrupt churn.
- Cost volatility: Uplift cap at 6% to limit downside; we propose an annual review tied to a published cost index (GPU hours + Azure pricing component).

Attachments: Nimbus_MAAP_Draft_v2.pdf (term summary + redlines)

Ask: Can I get a yes/no from both of you by EOD tomorrow? If yes, I’ll confirm with Legal and Procurement and send a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine —

Thanks for the concise summary. High level I support anchoring the rate for 36 months and the uplift cap (6% p.a.) given the strategic nature and upside. Two clarifying points before I fully sign off:

1) How do we measure \"committed spend\" for the >30% renewal escape? Is that based on annual contracted ACV or trailing 12-month invoiced spend?
2) Legal: I need a Legal thumbs-up on the escape clause wording so it can't be gamed for small dips. Please have Legal draft precise triggers (notification windows, calculation method).

If Legal confirms a strict definition and Finance is comfortable with recognition, I’m happy to approve.

-Vivek

Jasmine / Vivek —

Adding Finance perspective. My main concern is revenue recognition and downside at renewal if large customers exercise the escape clause. A few asks: 

- Can Sales provide a 3-year cashflow projection under the proposed uplift cap and the worst-case scenario where they exit at year 2? I started a small spreadsheet (attached: finance_notes.xlsx) for sensitivity modeling.
- If they opt for annual billing but leave mid-term, how do we treat prepaid credits / unused commitments? Recommend a clawback schedule or credit amortization that protects us.

If Sales can accept a limited clawback schedule (e.g., return of unused portion on a 12-month amortization) and the escape clause has a strict 60-day notice + proof of >30% decline in invoiced usage, I can provisionally approve. Legal to finalize.

-Markus

Thanks for the proposal and the draft MAAP. A few items from Procurement / Legal on our side: 

- We need confirmation that our enterprise SSO & data retention windows will be supported in the dedicated setup; please confirm SAML + 12 month logs retention.

Team — quick update and request to finalize: 

Status:
- Vivek: verbal OK on anchor + 6% comp cap pending Legal precise wording.
- Markus: provisional Finance approval pending clawback schedule; I’ve accepted the proposed amortization approach (12-mo pro-rata) to protect revenue.
- Nimbus: accepted the 6% cap but asked for non-compounding wording. They also asked for a pro-rated refund approach if they exercise escape.

What I’m sending to Legal now: final term sheet with the following agreed points to be drafted into contract language —
1) Rate anchor for 36 months.
2) Uplift cap: 6% p.a., non-compounding (per customer request). We will state the reference public index in the SOW.
3) Renewal escape: customer may exit if trailing 12-month invoiced spend is >=30% below contracted ACV at renewal. 60-day notice required. Unused prepaid months refunded on a 12-month straight-line amortization.

Next steps: Legal to produce the final redline and I’ll circulate a DocuSign. Can I get a final sign-off from both of you (Vivek + Markus) via reply-all by EOD Monday so Procurement can include the DocuSign link in their board packet?
